title: Check hashability before validating Categorical comparison lengths
answers: Why does comparing a Categorical with an iterator raise a TypeError about len()?
Should Categorical equality treat an iterator as a scalar or as elementwise values?
How should Categorical comparisons handle hashable list-like operands?
body:
Symptom: Comparing a Categorical with an iterator raises TypeError because the iterator has no length.
Root cause: pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py:_cat_compare_op evaluated len(other) before excluding hashable operands from the list-like length check.
Fix pattern: Short-circuit on non-hashability before checking list-likeness and length; hashable operands such as tuples and iterators take the scalar-like path.
Constraints: Apply length validation only to non-hashable list-like operands; mismatched lengths must still raise ValueError. pandas/tests/arrays/categorical/test_operators.py:TestCategoricalOps.test_comparison_with_iterator verifies that comparing Categorical(["a", "b"]) with iter(["a", "b"]) yields all False for == and all True for !=.
applies: Categorical comparison operand classification and length validation in _cat_compare_op.
